content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed tomato with rice is a dish where a ripe tomato is filled with a mixture of cooked rice, vegetables, and spices. The recipe is completely meat‑free, making it suitable for vegetarians and those following a plant‑based diet.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health.
Stuffing tomatoes is a tradition that dates back centuries in Mediterranean cuisine.
Rice in the filling adds bulk and provides lasting satiety.
The dish can be easily customized with different vegetables, nuts, or plant proteins.
Stuffed tomatoes are often served chilled in summer as a light appetizer.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes provide a substantial amount of vitamin C, which boosts the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Rice and vegetables supply dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The absence of meat and animal fats makes the dish heart‑friendly.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene in tomatoes helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Steady energy source
items.content: Complex carbohydrates from rice provide a stable release of energy without sharp blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, ranging from skin rashes to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salt is added to the filling, monitor the amount, especially for people with hypertension.

items.title: Risk of bacterial growth
items.content: Insufficient cooking can allow bacteria to survive. Ensure the dish reaches at least 75 °C during preparation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wash the tomatoes, carefully scoop out the core, cook rice until tender, mix it with finely chopped vegetables, herbs, and spices. Stuff the tomatoes, bake at 180 °C for 20‑25 minutes until softened. Serve warm or chilled, garnished with fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared stuffed tomatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a separate container for up to 2 months after cooling to room temperature.
